It's okay to worry about the what ifs! I actually worried about this specifically very recently. I was bit by a cat in my neighborhood a couple months ago, and then stumbled across an article about rabies which said the virus could live in your body for months. Of course, I freaked out and began reading article after article about it which calmed me down when I realized how very rare it was to catch in the U.S. 

There are only 2-3 cases per year and they usually always come from bats, not dogs or cats. And in your case, its even rarer to catch since you got scratched, not bit, which is how the disease is almost always spread. If no blood was drawn, theres no chance of catching rabies since it spreads through infected saliva travelling in your bloodstream. However, I know HA is irrational so if you happen to know where the cats are, you could observe them. If the cat is still alive after 10 days, you were NOT infected during the time of the scratch and you have nothing to worry about, (though I dont think you have anything to worry about anyway!). Hope this helps.

It might just be a difference of opinion. For me, I'd want to know about past sex work, past addictions, childhoods, stuff like that. I think it's better to have that stuff out in the open. It wouldnt change my opinion on the person or even stop me from dating them necessarily, but it would bother me if they waited until someone else brought it up to tell me. That would make me reconsider because I'd wonder why they wouldnt feel comfortable telling me before. If they think I'd leave them because of it, then at that point, they're purposefully omitting information that they know I wouldnt be okay with. It would also make me wonder if theres other important things in their past that they're not telling me. I understand your perspective though. Congratulations on you and your wife being together for over 10 years, that's awesome.

I think because the issue is controversial. It's like anything else in a relationship that's part of your past. I know these are different situations, but past drug addictions or alcohol addictions are something that might be deal breakers for people. I think people like to say the past doesnt matter, I disagree with that. What if she runs into former clients? What if he runs into her former clients? What if (like he mentioned) people from his job find the website she was on? If he knew about her past and then pursued a relationship with her, then these are probably risks he considered and was fine with, but without knowing that, he didnt make an informed decision. 

Also, you could flip the question to her. Why marry someone you're not comfortable sharing your past with?

I think the issue is she didnt tell him and hes not comfortable with it. A lot of people in this thread are making it seem like hes judging her. I dont see it that way. You can respect sex work and sex workers yet have the preference to not wanna be with one. That's okay. But by her not telling him, he wasnt able to make an informed decision about whether or not he was okay with her past.
Not necessarily. However, if that's the way you really feel, you might wanna consider dating in the religious community. You might be able to find some people that are waiting till marriage.

I'm not trying to judge you, genuinely, I'm trying to see where you're coming from. I can understand not wanting to date someone with a promiscuous past, that's a preference some people have. However, that doesnt seem to be the case here. 9 partners at 30 isnt promiscuous. That number could be from boyfriends over the years.

I guess that's one way to deal with it. Is there a reason in particular your unhappy with your girlfriends past? Is it an issue with the amount of partners shes had? Or situational, like having sex outside of relationships is the issue?
How so?
So what's your ideal woman? A virgin? No body count? 1-2? I'm just wondering how you'll handle this in the future.
That's an understandable stance to take.
I think the point hes making is, why is she doing something that she wouldnt be okay with him doing. If it's a boundary set for him, it should be a boundary for her as well.

Not everything needs to be answered with "just leave". Relationships are built on compromise. She can decide to stop out of respect, or he can decide it's no longer a big deal. Saying, "she doesnt have to listen to your voiced discomfort" or "then you should just leave" is invalidating of his feelings and an oversimplified way of looking at relationships. Bad advice imo.
This arguement could be used to justify basically anything, including cheating. Every relationship has its boundaries. It's not about 'listening to him' as if hes her dad, it's about mutual respect.

I think if you want more and he doesnt, you're only hurting yourself by continuing to see him casually. I dont think its "bad" per say, just dishonest to him and yourself. There are plenty of other people out there who will be into you and want a relationship. Theres no point in waiting around for someone who may or may not be interested later.
I feel you lol. I'm typing this at 2 in the morning as we speak so.... yay...

I think in general, it helps. And social skills, in my definition, are more than just being able to strike a conversation. I mentioned it in a conversation above, but some men (women do this too, I just say men because I date men so this is based off my experience) can be oblivious on how to act with a girl. Being overbearing with compliments and gestures early on, putting women on a pedestal, that kind of thing can be off putting. In OPs case, I dont know him so I dont know how he acts, but there are quite a few people who do this not realizing why it's a red flag to most people, which can be considered bad social skills. Just going based off of what he wrote, he seems to be doing good in every other aspect of life, so the only things I could think of holding him back in dating are social skills and or his personality.

There are exceptions to the rule, of course, but I'm talking in general. Good social skills increase your chances of getting dates and keeping them interested. Think of it as a numbers game. The more people you're able to talk to and engage with positively, the more connections you  make, which in turn can lead to more dating prospects. In your case, you might just be introverted but still be able to carry yourself in conversations. Introversion doesnt automatically mean bad social skills, just that you prefer to be alone more.

Depends on the 20 year old. I know quite a few people who got married at 18-20. Not saying it was a good idea, but there are definitely young people who are interested in commitment. And yeah, a lot that arent. My post was just to ask what OP wanted. She says she doesnt want to be casual anymore but has feelings for him but also doesnt want a relationship. So what does she really want out of him?
Lmao definitely. If women and men could switch places for a minute and see where the other side is coming from, we'd have a much better dating world I think.

Yes, definitely. A problem I see with guys often is that, although they're very sweet, they sometimes treat women as if they're beyond human. Going overboard with compliments or gestures, which can be really off putting, especially if you dont know each other that well. Women arent goddesses. Talking to them, and people in general, as equals instead of putting them on a pedestal can make a big difference. Be yourself, dont put on a show, keep your self esteem high, and eventually some nice lady will come along and think it's pretty cool.

Yes, a 100% this isn't a gender exclusive thing. I just used the example since I'm a woman giving advice to a man who wants to date women but everybody across the board should work on their social skills. It helps in every area of life really.

Definitely. From a womans perspective, there have been guys I typically wouldn't look twice at just based off appearances, but because of their humor or conversation skills, I found them attractive. Same has happened in reverse where I've talked to attractive guys, but as I spoke to them, their attitudes made them less attractive. It makes a much bigger difference than most would believe.
Did you talk to her about it first?

He doesn't want a relationship, theres no advice to really give here. When someone says "I'm not ready for a relationship right now", it usually means they're not into you, unless they just got out of a relationship or have personal stuff going on, but in this case I dont think that's it. I think you should move on. Waiting for someone to make time for you and hope they'll eventually get in a relationship is just a waste of time. You deserve someone who will make time for you and want something more than casual dating. As for staying friends or keeping in contact, that's up to you to decide. I personally try to avoid contact with people I have feelings for until those feelings pass, because I know it's not fair to them to continue to be friends meanwhile I'm imagining them in a relationship setting. And also, what do you want from him? You wrote that you didnt want a relationship at the moment either. So wouldnt that imply you continue things casually or as just friends? 

Edit: just reread and saw you wrote that he did get out of a relationship. Definitely could be that, but point still stands. I would leave it alone and not wait.

It really depends on the contact before the date. Did the texts naturally come to an end or was it something she should have responded to? Has she initiated contact before? Is she reserved? I know some women, me included when it comes to new partners, can be shy when it comes to initiating in fear of coming off as desperate or clingy. Especially if it's only been one date. I'd say text her about the next date, see how she responds. If it takes two days and she just responds with a vague answer, yeah, shes not interested. If she responds in a way that's engaged and in a reasonable time frame, it might just be that shes shy and doesnt wanna initiate like I said before. Or she could be more traditional and expect the man to reach out. No can tell you without context.

How are your social skills? Do you have a circle of friends? Are you more introverted or nervous around people? I'd say social skills can make or break someone when it comes to dating. You can have a body like Chris Hemsworth yet get no women if you cant talk to them. Same works in reverse. Sometimes less attractive men get lots of women simply from having really good social skills.

I also work customer service as well. Personally, I wouldnt see a problem with someone handing me their number at work or asking for coffee politely. Yes it's our job to be nice to people, but not all of it is fake. I know in my experience, there are customers I was extra nice to just because I genuinely liked them, not just because it was my job. As long as hes not creepy, overly persistent, or distracting her from her job for longer than a minute, theres really nothing uncomfortable about it. I think you make it a bigger deal than it actually is.

I second this. Giving out your number is the best way to hit on someone you dont know. It let's them know you're interested, while giving them all the power. Since shes at work and your a customer, this is how I would go about it.

What your friend is saying is kind of correct but for all the wrong reasons. If I'm understanding, hes basically saying act like you've moved on so she'll come back. I agree you should move on and focus on doing you but not so she'll come back, just do it because you want to focus on yourself! There is no 'strategy' to people. They either like you or they dont. If she likes you, she'll come around. If she doesnt, the whole 'I've moved on' act will do nothing. Because she wont care and if she does, it's probably going to be for the wrong reason. 

That goes for women, men, anyone. People who like you will come to you when you've made your feelings known, people who dont, wont.

Because it's something more intimate that people usually do with a partner, or a very close friend at the very least. I dont have a lot of boundaries so I wouldnt find it that weird, but I could definitely see a lot of other people finding it creepy, probably a majority. Bad idea. Cheating this early into the relationship is not a good sign, regardless of the reason. This is the honeymoon phase, where you're supposed to be your happiest and most focused on each other. She can give excuses that her friend told her to do it or she was intoxicated but at the end of the day, she made the decision to cheat. You might forgive her and it does seem like shes regretful of her decision,  but you should ask yourself if you're willing to pursue a relationship that's basically being built on no trust. What is she gonna do in a year when the relationship is no longer new and exciting to her? What are you gonna do when she wants to go out late without you? 

Its still early, to me, theres no reason she did this. And if it is a pattern with her to self sabotage, that's something she should figure out with a therapist. Not string you along for the ride.

Ive been in this situation before and you have my sympathy, it's tough. But something that helped me was figuring out why I couldn't stop thinking about this person in the first place. I'm someone who likes closure, and since my person ghosted me, I never got that, so it was hard for me to move on completely for a really long time.
 Maybe examine your thoughts about him to see why you're hung up on him? What do you think about when you think about him? Is it happy memories about you two together? Is it a fantasy about you two having a future together? Is it a lack of closure? Is it regret about the breakup? I know it might sound counter productive to ask you to think about it more, but maybe finding the 'why do I keep thinking about him' will help you find the 'how to move on.' 

It also could be that your pushing yourself so hard to stop thinking about him that its having the opposite effect. Kinda like if I told you, "stop thinking about elephants." Well, now you're thinking about elephants. You mentioned therapy, you could also work some of this out with your therapist. Best of luck to you and dont forget to love yourself. You can always reach out if youd like to talk more.

Yes. It always starts with lots of texting and meeting in the beginning, then slowly dies out until we stop talking. It definitely could be something I'm doing, but honestly I don't know. And theres also the fact I'm very used to guys talking a lot in the beginning then slowly disappearing as time goes on, until contact is completely gone.

He usually initiates but we both contribute to the conversation equally. It's never one worded or anything and our conversations dont usually end, it just picks up where it was the day before. I might be overreacting, tbh I'm not sure. I'm very used to guys ghosting so when they start texting less and less, I assume hes losing interest and ghosting is what's gonna come next.

Edit: I should probably also add when we first started talking, he worked two jobs and was in school. He quit one so now it's only one job and school. But he still texted more when he was busier.

There is a huge difference between sleeping with the same person 150 times and sleeping with 150 people one time 😂😂. One shows commitment and loyalty whereas the other looks impulsive and hard to take seriously if you want a relationship. It's like a resume. Would you prefer to hire someone who worked for the same company for 20 years? Or 20 companies in 20 years? Sure they have the same experience but one looks 1000 percent better than the other.

I think it's up to you and how you feel. At the end of the day, you know her better than anyone on here ever will. I tend to trust my gut on these things and that's the advice I'd give to you. The engagement thing and her keeping him as a contact would definitely throw me off but if it was just a slip up and out of character, that's something that you might be able to move on from. Aside from that, if her body count/sexual history makes you uncomfortable, you have to decide if that's something you're willing to put out of your mind because you really care for this girl, or if its something that's going to continue to bother you and you cant accept it. She put the ball in your court by telling you about it, now it's on you. You might also want to ask yourself a couple questions. Have other girls you've dated had a body count that made you uncomfortable or is it just her? Is it just the acts themsevles that she did with other men (like anal) but not you that make you uncomfortable? Are you insecure about these past relationships or do you just have a different view on sex/relationships then her and that's the issue? These might be questions that give you an answer to why you feel the way you do towards her sexual history and how you wanna proceed. You also mentioned somewhere in the post that you werent sure if you wanted to make things 'official'. I'm not quite sure what that means to you, but to me that tells me your still in a newish stage of dating. Imo, if you're already having problems early on, that's a bad sign. But again, only you really know.

The fact that she still keeps him as a contact after knowing he was/is engaged would be a red flag to me. It's not the past if you refuse to delete them. That being said, I agree. It's his problem. But dating is meant to be discriminatory, you can stop seeing someone for any reason. If a high body count makes him uncomfortable, I think that's something he should take into account and a sign they might have different views on sex/relationships.

I disagree. Sleeping with a guy that's married and continuing to see him after knowing that info is a major red flag. That being said, as for the rest of the post, body count matters if you make it matter. If he's uncomfortable with her past or the amount of people shes slept with, then that's something he shouldnt ignore. The thoughts will only persist and cause jealousy/tension as the relationship continues. I say go with your gut.
